scope: Narrative review of acute-on-chronic neuromuscular respiratory failure, written around ALS patients without a tracheostomy.

keyRecommendations.text: Acute respiratory failure requiring intubation commonly leads to tracheostomy or palliative-focused care.
New hypoxia and hypercapnia are not initially presumed to be end-stage neuromuscular failure.
Selected patients may need intubation or advanced NIV adjustments.

clinicalBottomLine: Look for a new cause of hypoxia or hypercapnia before calling the episode end-stage disease. Some patients need intubation or a change in NIV; many who are intubated proceed to tracheostomy or a palliative plan.
notableCaveats: No numeric vital-capacity threshold is stated in the sentences used, so none is taught.

source.title: Acute on Chronic Neuromuscular Respiratory Failure in the Intensive Care Unit: A Narrative Review.
